assessment: Selection errors, layout confusion and mixed-order delays suggest a shared handoff hypothesis; the observations do not establish their causes. One integrated opening is offered, with cost and deadline feasibility unresolved.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: adapt a tool shadow board into a reusable order-specific kitting mat, then carry its partition-to-position mapping onto the existing order slip for customer setup. Keep workshop assembly initially so any gain comes from selection and handoff changes.
openings.delta: Parent mechanisms are occupancy-based completeness checking and position-based assembly guidance, crossed at a shared partition identifier. Together they could detect omissions while explaining the short partition's destination. Failed correspondence: tool boards have fixed inventories; these orders vary in count and color, and similar partitions may be indistinguishable by outline. Change the material assumption to interchangeable paper overlays on spare board, with quantity and orientation labels; check exterior color separately. Repurpose the existing order slip's order identity as the link between selected contents and ordered layout. Its presence is supplied; readable layout annotation is a new enabling dependency. Existing cutting templates supply candidate outlines, whose correspondence to actual parts must be checked before use.
openings.prediction: The linked pair should reduce selection/checking time and short-partition placement errors more than either aid alone, without increasing insertion time or changing the product.
openings.probe: Use up to 15 sample sets for counterbalanced worker trials of baseline, mat alone, slip alone and linked aids across layouts; time each activity and seed recoverable omissions or substitutions. Have ten participants attempt their ordered arrangement using paired slip conditions with order counterbalanced; treat results as exploratory. Before adoption, cost preparation and annotations against both caps and the fixed deadline. Then measure the 60-order pilot: at least 59 complete orders, median time at most eight minutes, and customer success against the 90% target.
assumptions: Preparation and annotation fit the spending and delivery limits.
Original parts, footprint, capacity, removable joints, accepted counts and colors are retained.
